newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka tea prices ease as bigger supplies seen.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka tea prices ease as bigger supplies seen.

text.p: Sri Lankan tea prices fell at auction on Wednesday after the weekly average price hit a record last week and buyers held back in anticipation of bigger supplies ahead, brokers said.
"The market is slightly overheated," said a broker at Forbes and Walker. "Also, buyers know there are bigger volumes available in the weeks ahead."
The estimated auction average price for the 4.4 million kg of tea on offer fell to 122.50 rupees per kg ($2.15) from a record 123.71 rupees last week, he said.
"We could see a turning point in the next week or so because of increasing volumes," said a broker at Eastern Brokers. "The market appears to have peaked for the current period."
Brokers said tea prices have been soaring in recent weeks because of the classic combination of higher demand and lower quantities.
The next auction is on October 22-23 where 4.9 million kg will be on offer.
